newsitem.title: SPAIN: Catalans reluctantly back Spain 1997 budget - paper.
newsitem.headline: Catalans reluctantly back Spain 1997 budget - paper.

text.p: Catalan coalition leader Jordi Pujol has reluctantly agreed to back the Spanish government's 1997 budget, newspaper El Pais reported on Tuesday.

But his Convergence and Unity coalition, whose support of the minority Popular Party government is essential for the PP to remain in government, has threatened to stop backing the Popular Party over disagreements over financing health spending in the budget, the report said.

According to El Pais, Pujol told Economy Minister Rodrigo Rato that said his party's backing for the central government and Spain's political stability would be affected if the CiU is obliged to vote for the budget draft as it stands.
Senior coalition members said Pujol "isn't bluffing," El Pais reported.
CiU meets for a new round of negotiations with the government in Madrid today, the paper said.
